message: No detected input validation: No schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards are performed on the CSV data read by FileReader or on the query parameters beyond the basic type conversion via to_date.
No detected untrusted source handling: Data is read from local CSV files via FileReader/Path with no checksum verification, authentication, or integrity checks on the source.
No detected label flipping detection: No code checks label distributions, validates label values against an expected set, or uses any label-noise detection tool before training.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The preparation pipeline (Scaler, FileReader, Db) performs only date/time splitting and column dropping with no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious inputs.

No detected model integrity verification: Models are trained in-memory at startup from scratch and never serialized or loaded from disk, so there is no hash check, signature verification, or controlled-source loading implemented.

No detected label distribution validation: No code checks class balance, label distribution, or anomalous samples before or during training; the pipeline reads CSV data and passes it directly to model fitting.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation analysis, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training loop or supporting code.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy library (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD, etc.) is imported or applied during training.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing libraries or techniques (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) are used anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: While a train/test split is performed, the test set is not cryptographically protected or hashed, only a single metric (R2 score) is used, and there is no isolation guarantee preventing leakage between training and evaluation data.

No detected input sanitization: The endpoints parse 'from' and 'to' query params via to_date() for format enforcement, but there is no validation of input shape, range, or feature values before passing data to the model.
No detected output bounds checks: Predictions from model.predict() are returned directly without any NaN guards, range checks, or sanity bounds on the predicted flow values.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is not an LLM pipeline; it uses sklearn regressors (DecisionTree, GradientBoosting, RandomForest), so prompt injection defenses are not applicable.
